A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPECMIND research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original EvalPlus effectiveness, reasoning, feedback, and cost experiments in Section 6, plus FixEval bug-detection results in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical studies, moves FixEval results into Section 6.5, and adds original GLM-4.7 results in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The algorithm, feedback procedures, history buffer, submission tracking, stopping behavior, and prompt template remain unchanged. The four design ideas added to Section 2 summarize components already documented in v1, particularly Sections 4–5 and Figures 2–3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate postcondition generation on EvalPlus and bug detection on FixEval. Moving FixEval into RQ5 adds no task or dataset coverage; GLM-4.7 introduces another model configuration within the existing coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain single-pass nl2postcond, independent random sampling with nl2postcond, Greedy, and Exploratory. The new GLM-4.7 table uses the same comparison methods. TestWeaver is cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 extends the existing RQ1 evaluation grid to GLM-4.7, retaining completeness thresholds of 50, 70, and 90 and turn budgets of 4, 8, and 12. The earlier Llama and FixEval protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The GLM-4.7 evaluation adds a limited check of whether the main effectiveness pattern persists with another underlying LLM. The reasoning analysis, enhanced-feedback hard-case experiment, completeness trajectories, and illustrative case studies are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: The new results retain point-estimate reporting without additional seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures. The existing FixEval statement about sampling 384 bugs with 95% statistical significance is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds a substantial parallel results grid for GLM-4.7, including single-pass correctness/completeness of 46.0%/12.4% and Exploratory results of 99.37%/87.57% at threshold 90 and budget 12. These are additional model-specific results; the original Llama results, FixEval scores, and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The postcondition definitions, correctness and completeness criteria, inference objective, history formulation, and efficiency equation are unchanged. The expanded design discussion introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about interactive exploratory reasoning, autonomous stopping, specification quality, and bug-detection benefits remain substantively unchanged. The design summary and RQ5 heading emphasize contributions already present in v1.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning refinement, escaping local optima, history, stopping, and cost tradeoffs are retained. The new design summary restates that rationale, while limitations concerning generalization, pretraining exposure, test coverage, and mutant quality remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code/data availability statement in the introduction and a SpecMind code repository reference, absent from v1. It does not add substantial implementation, hardware, or execution instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds TestWeaver (Le et al., 2026) to the related-work discussion of test coverage. The Speculyzer citation changes from Key et al. (2022) to Li et al. (2025), while retaining the same described method and positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a four-part design summary, promotes the existing FixEval study to Section 6.5/RQ5, separates its example into Appendix A.6, and adjusts headings, wording, and author information. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the GLM-4.7 table and reformats the relocated FixEval Table 3 into a compact single-column display. Existing figures retain their content, while floats move and the reasoning-trajectory table becomes Table 5.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone evaluation, code/data reference, and clearer organization modestly improve empirical support and assessability. The gains are limited: GLM-4.7 settings receive little explanation, and its entire attempt/submission columns exactly match the Llama table without explanation. These reporting issues limit the strength of the added evidence; the original results and uncertainty-reporting limitations remain.
